title: Length-Indexed First Halting Times
statement: Let $M$ be a finite deterministic machine over the binary alphabet, let $f$ assign a binary word to each natural number, and let $T$ assign a natural-number time bound to each natural number. Suppose that for every $n$, $M$ computes $f(n)$ within $T(n)$ steps on the all-ones word of length $n$. Then there is a function $\tau$ from the natural numbers to the natural numbers such that, for every binary word $x$, $\tau(|x|)\le T(|x|)$, the input-normalized machine associated with $M$ computes $f(|x|)$ within $\tau(|x|)$ steps on $x$, and the machine is not halted at any time $s<\tau(|x|)$ in that computation.
